original_title: Final Fantasy 7 Director Kept 'Open World Fatigue' in Mind as New Remake Chapter Promises 'Bigger' World Than Rebirth

en.title: Final Fantasy 7 Director Confirms 'Open World Fatigue' Focus for Remake's Finale
en.summary: The director of the upcoming Final Fantasy 7 Remake chapter, Naoki Hamaguchi, is acutely aware of player burnout from sprawling open worlds. He assures fans that the finale will offer ample guidance, even as it promises a world larger than its predecessor.
en.body:
The final chapter of the **Final Fantasy 7** Remake saga is on the horizon, and director **Naoki Hamaguchi** is keenly aware of a growing trend in the gaming industry: open-world fatigue. In a recent conversation with Eurogamer, Hamaguchi addressed concerns that massive, sprawling environments can sometimes overwhelm players, leaving them feeling lost and unsure of their next steps. He emphasized that the development team at Square Enix has been "very careful" to ensure that players in the upcoming game, tentatively titled **Final Fantasy 7 Revelation**, will always have "all the guidance they need."

This focus on player direction comes even as the new installment is set to offer a world that is "bigger" than that of **Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth**. The previous two games, **Final Fantasy 7 Remake** and **Rebirth**, have been praised for their detailed worlds but have also been part of wider discussions about the sheer scale of modern open-world titles. Hamaguchi acknowledged this sentiment, stating, "There are a lot of open world games out in the world right now, and [the idea of 'open world fatigue'] is a very important concept to me." He shared his own experiences of feeling adrift in large game worlds, noting, "I know I've had the experience where I've been thrown out into an open world game and not known where to go, not known where to begin, and not known what to do."

## Balancing Freedom and Direction

Despite the potential for players to feel lost, Hamaguchi also recognizes the inherent appeal of a truly expansive and wondrous world. "But at the same time, the concept of being thrown into this wondrous world where anything goes is amazing," he commented. For a game like **Final Fantasy 7 Revelation**, which is expected to be packed with content, the allure of getting lost in its vibrant universe is undeniable. The key, as Hamaguchi sees it, lies in striking the right balance. As a creator, he believes it's crucial to "offer proper guidance" within these vast landscapes, ensuring that the player's journey remains engaging and purposeful without sacrificing the sense of discovery.

## What This Means for Fans

This commitment to thoughtful design is a significant point for long-time fans of **Final Fantasy 7**. The series has always been celebrated for its compelling narrative and characters, and the desire to experience Cloud's final confrontation with Sephiroth without getting bogged down by endless waypoints or aimless exploration will be a welcome assurance. The **Final Fantasy 7 Remake** project is a monumental undertaking, aiming to deliver the beloved story with modern fidelity and gameplay. Hearing that the developers are actively considering player experience and potential burnout suggests a mature approach to concluding this epic trilogy, prioritizing a satisfying narrative conclusion over sheer scale for its own sake.

## What's Next

While a specific release date for **Final Fantasy 7 Revelation** has not yet been announced, Square Enix has previously targeted a 2027 launch. Fans can anticipate further details and gameplay previews in the coming months as the development team gears up for the finale of this ambitious remake.

tr.title: Final Fantasy 7 Remake'in Son Bölümünde 'Açık Dünya Yorgunluğu' Odaklanacak
tr.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Remake'in son bölümünün yönetmeni Naoki Hamaguchi, oyuncuların açık dünya oyunlarından kaynaklanan yorgunluğunun farkında ve son bölümde oyunculara yeterli rehberlik sağlanacağını söylüyor. Bu, daha büyük bir dünya vaat ederken aynı zamanda oyuncuların kaybolmasını önlemek için tasarlandı.
tr.body:
## Açık Dünya Yorgunluğu
Final Fantasy 7 Remake'in son bölümü yaklaşıyor ve yönetmen Naoki Hamaguchi, oyun endüstrisinde giderek artan bir trend olan açık dünya yorgunluğunun farkında. Eurogamer ile yaptığı recent bir konuşmada Hamaguchi, devasa açık dünya ortamlarının bazen oyuncuları boğabileceğini ve onlara próximo adımlarını belirlemede zorluk yaşatabileceğini ifade etti. Square Enix'in geliştirme ekibinin, oyunculara her zaman ihtiyaç duydukları rehberliği sağlayarak 'her şeyi görebilecekleri' bir dünya yaratmaya çalıştıklarını vurguladı.

## Özgürlük ve Yönlendirme Arasındaki Denge
Hamaguchi, oyuncuların kaybolabileceği potansiyeline rağmen, gerçekten geniş ve harika bir dünyanın çekiciliğini de tanımaktadır. 'Ama aynı zamanda, her şeyin mümkün olduğu harika bir dünyaya atılmak inanılmaz bir şey,' diye yorumladı. Final Fantasy 7 Revelation gibi içeriği bol bir oyun için, bu geniş evrenin içinde kaybolmanın çekiciliği inkar edilemez. Anahtar, Hamaguchi'ye göre, doğru dengeyi bulmakta yatmaktadır. Bir yaratıcı olarak, bu geniş manzaralar içinde 'uygun rehberlik' sunmanın önemine inanmaktadır, böylece oyuncunun yolculuğu ilgi çekici ve amaçlı kalırken, keşif duygusundan ödün vermemektedir.

## Bu, Hayranlar için Ne Anlama Geliyor
Dikkatli bir tasarıma olan bu bağlılık, uzun süredir Final Fantasy 7 serisinin hayranları için önemli bir noktadır. Seri, her zaman çekici bir anlatı ve karakterler ile kutlanmıştır ve Cloud'un Sephiroth ile final karşılaşmasını sonsuz waypoint'ler veya amaçsız keşiflerle boğulmadan deneyimlemek isteyeceklerdir. Final Fantasy 7 Remake projesi, sevgili hikayeyi modern bir şekilde ve oyun oynama deneyimi ile sunmayı hedefleyen devasa bir girişimdir. Geliştiricilerin oyuncuların deneyimini ve potansiyel yorgunluğunu aktif olarak dikkate aldıklarını duymak, bu epik üçlemenin závěresini, salt ölçek için değil, tatmin edici bir anlatı sonunu önceliklendiren olgereksin bir yaklaşımı göstermektedir.

## Sonraki Adımlar
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation için específik bir yayın tarihi henüz açıklanmasa da, Square Enix daha önce 2027 lanç için hedeflemişti. Hayranlar, geliştirme ekibinin finale hazırlanırken, gelecek aylarda daha fazla ayrıntı ve oyun ön izlemesi bekleyebilirler.

content_raw: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi has acknowledged the "open world fatigue" affecting the industry but says Square Enix was "very careful" to make sure fans would have "all the guidance they need" in the new remake chapter – even if it's bigger than the last. The developer helping lead the finale to its 2027 launch spoke about its size during a conversation with Eurogamer . In the interview, he teased how the team has done its best to tie a bow on the trilogy with one final adventure for Cloud, Tifa, Barret, and the rest of the gang in their fight against Sephiroth . The two previous installments in the remake trilogy – Final Fantasy 7 Remake and Rebirth – have been lumped into online conversations about enormous open worlds that sometimes overstay their welcome. Hamaguchi said the concept of open world fatigue is "very important" to him, but it sounds like players won't need to worry about feeling too lost. "There are a lot of open world games out in the world right now, and [the idea of 'open world fatigue'] is a very important concept to me," he replied when Eurogamer asked about feedback to Rebirth. "It depends on personal preference and different perceptions, but for me personally, I know I've had the experience where I've been thrown out into an open world game and not known where to go, not known where to begin, and not known what to do. But at the same time, the concept of being thrown into this wondrous world where anything goes is amazing." There are certainly players who would prefer to get lost in a vibrant fantasy universe. In a world promising to be as packed as Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, that idea might be especially enticing. Hamaguchi said that, as a creator, he believes it's important to "offer proper guidance" in open-world games so that players "know what to do, and know where to go." "In Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, we made sure to make it easy for the players to understand how much content there is, and how difficult that content is," he added. "That design philosophy is applied to Revelation: players have all the guidance that they need. This is something that both myself and the development team were very careful about when we designed the game." It seems Hamaguchi and the rest of the development team wanted to strike a balance when it came to guidance in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. One example he mentioned involved asking players to rely on their memory to make sure they land in their desired location when dropping from the Highwind airship . "That's another example of the guidance we're giving players, without directing them too much," Hamaguchi continued. "The world is even bigger than it was in Rebirth, so it is more important than ever for us to ensure there's enough guidance here, so people have no issues enjoying what this game has to offer."
